title: Remembering the Good Done to You
note: This is not forgetting the good others have done you. It follows sweet speech because, for those who keep household righteousness, the one fault with no escape is destroying a kindness, and this guards against it.

couplets.plain: For help you did nothing to earn, even earth and sky are hardly a fair return.
couplets.pm: For help a person gives when you had done them no good first, even earth and heaven given in return can hardly match it. Every return has a cause, so none can match help with no cause. Some read a variant that makes this help given where it can’t be repaid.

links.quote: even earth and sky are hardly a fair return

couplets.plain: A good deed done at the right time, though small, is far greater than the world.
couplets.pm: Help given when someone’s end has come may be small in itself, but judged by that moment it is far greater than the earth. You should look at the moment, not at the thing given.

links.quote: A good deed done at the right time
links.reason: Measures a good deed by its timing, not by its size.

links.quote: though small, is far greater than the world

couplets.plain: Weigh the goodness of help given with no thought of return, and it is greater than the sea.
couplets.pm: If you weigh the kindness in help given by those who never ask what it will bring, its goodness is greater than the sea. These three couplets say that help given without cause, at the right time, or without thought of return is boundless.

links.quote: help given with no thought of return

links.reason: Needs the sea as the only thing big enough to compare with such help.

couplets.plain: Though the good done them is the size of a millet seed, those who know its worth take it as the size of a palmyra.
couplets.pm: Though someone does them a good the size of a millet seed, those who know what comes of thinking so take it as the size of a palmyra. Millet and palmyra are the usual measures of small and large.

links.reason: Those who know its worth see a small good as something towering.

links.quote: the size of a millet seed
take it as the size of a palmyra

couplets.plain: The measure of help is not the help itself. It is the worth of those who received it.
couplets.pm: The help given back isn’t measured by the earlier help, in its cause, substance or timing. It is measured by the character of those who received that help. As great as their character is, so great is the help. These two couplets say that even ordinary help is great when done to those who know its worth.

links.quote: the worth of those who received it
links.reason: Says the measure is set by the worth of the receiver and not by the size of the help.

couplets.plain: Don’t forget the bond of the stainless. Don’t give up the friendship of those who stood by you in trouble.
couplets.pm: Don’t give up the friendship of those who were your support in trouble. Don’t forget the bond of those without fault in knowledge and conduct. Along with what serves you in this life, he names what serves you in the next.

links.quote: Don’t give up the friendship of those who stood by you in trouble
Don’t forget the bond of the stainless
links.reason: Asks that the bond with the stainless never be forgotten.

links.quote: those who stood by you in trouble

couplets.plain: Through seven lives and seven births, people remember the friendship of those who wiped away their sorrow.
couplets.pm: The good remember the friendship of those who removed their sorrow, through all seven kinds of birth, in the seven births that the fruit of deeds follows. “Wiped” shows how quickly it was done. To remember is for the loving-kindness felt for them to go on birth after birth.

links.quote: those who wiped away their sorrow

couplets.plain: It is not good to forget a good deed. It is good to forget what is not good, that very day.
couplets.pm: Forgetting the good someone did you before isn’t righteous. Forgetting the harm that same person did you, at the moment it is done, is righteous. This sorts what to forget and what to keep, when one person has done both.
couplets.sensitive: counsels forgetting an injury at once; could reach someone being mistreated

links.quote: It is not good to forget a good deed
links.reason: Says forgetting a good deed is not good.

links.quote: forget what is not good, that very day

couplets.plain: Though someone hurts you as if they were killing you, it all dies when you recall one good thing they did.
couplets.pm: If someone who once did you good later does you harm equal to killing you, all of it vanishes when you think of that one good. A millet seed of good is taken as a palmyra, so that one good destroys it all. This tells how to forget harm that very day.
couplets.sensitive: asks the gravely injured to forgive for one past kindness; could reach someone abused

links.quote: when you recall one good thing they did

couplets.plain: Those who have killed any good may still escape. There is no escape for the man who killed the good done to him.
couplets.pm: Those who wreck great righteous acts still have a way out of their sin. The man who wrecks a good done to him has none. Wrecking great righteousness means crimes such as cutting a cow’s udder, destroying a woman’s unborn child and killing Brahmins. This tells how terrible it is to kill a kindness.

links.quote: There is no escape for the man who killed the good done to him

ideaLinks.quote: it all dies when you recall one good thing they did
ideaLinks.reason: Recalling one good deed is enough to end even the worst hurt.
